liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Music Never Stopped** (3 reviews, 1 other source): Weir begins the first verse before Garcia delivers his introductory line; Weir, Keith and the drummers start out of sync; Keith later seems to push ahead of the beat [5][17][18][19]
- **Candyman** (2 reviews): Garcia's vocals are singled out as excellent, with Candyman described as spot on; The band can be heard laughing after Candyman ends, and Garcia's singing is praised [12][16]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review, 1 other source): Franklin's Tower is highlighted as part of a hot, dance-friendly performance; A dropout near the end of Franklin's Tower required a patch in the soundboard copy [2][15]
- **Brown Eyed Women** (1 review): The drummer plays against the beat, making the song lurch and stutter while Jerry keeps the tempo [20]
- **All Over Now** (1 review): It starts very quiet and keeps tightening until a runaway-train finish; Keith and Jerry interact closely on the second solo break after the 'run around' verse [21]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): Cassidy is recommended as a highlight for Jerry's performance [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **Salt Lake City**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **deer story**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-04-10.bbd.15782.shnf** (recommended): source not stated; 21 songs; 178 min; rated 4.71/5 by 7 [1]
- **gd1978-04-10.senn421.zimmerman.minches.81262.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 187 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [2]. Said about its sound: Levels were set too high, making the Nak shut down briefly; most of the encore was not captured [2]
- **gd78-04-10.sbd.miller.18098.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 177 min; rated 3.67/5 by 24 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer, who was at the show, finds the recording's sound quality electric; Reviewer hears faint crackle, clipped songs and volume problems, and deleted the show rather than fix it; The mix is clear enough that the band's laughter after Candyman is audible [12][14][16]
- **gd1978-04-10.148538.betty.dalton.miller.sirmick.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 176 min; rated 3/5 by 3 [5]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended this Fox Theater show as their first Dead concert and recalls it sounding similar on tape [10]
- Long tuning breaks interrupt the show's rhythm, though the theater atmosphere and band pleased the reviewer [19]
- Reviewer senses a mischievous mood throughout the performance [20]
- Reviewer prefers the following night's show over this one [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-04-10.bbd.15782.shnf**: source: Jace's source tape: MR>P1>D1 [1]. Also: Two Betty Board tapes cover the Fox Theatre shows of 10 and 11 April 1978; Not official WBOTB masters; uploader thinks there is an extra analog generation [1]
- **gd1978-04-10.senn421.zimmerman.minches.81262.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Alan Zimmerman; transferred by David Minches; source: 2 Sennheiser 421s (or 441s) + Sony 54P> passed through Nakamichi 550> Teac PC-10 (Maxell UD XLII-90s) [2]. Also: Audience recording made with a three-microphone setup feeding a Nak 550 [2]
- **gd78-04-10.sbd.miller.18098.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Soundboard transferred through Rm and PCM to DAT by Charlie Miller [3]
- **gd1978-04-10.148538.betty.dalton.miller.sirmick.flac16**: taped by Betty Cantor;Tim Dalton; transferred by Sirmick and Charlie Miller; source: Source: SBD Master Reel (7" two track @ 7 1/2 ips - recorded by Betty Cantor) > PCM501ES @ 44.055 kHz > DAT (44k) - From the Tim Dalton collection. [5]. Also: The Music Never Stopped and Franklin's Tower are patched from the Zimmerman and Minches audience source, shnid 81262 [5]
